what_it_does: Running large language models efficiently requires compressing their numbers from the standard 16-bit or 8-bit floating-point format down to 4-bit integers — a process called quantization — which reduces how much memory is needed and speeds up the multiplications. Modern GPUs have specialized math units built for 4-bit integer arithmetic, but quantizing both the stored model weights and the live intermediate values (activations) to 4 bits simultaneously causes noticeable accuracy loss because some of those intermediate values are unusually large "outliers" that cannot be squeezed into 4 bits without error. COMET addresses this by using a mixed-precision approach: it stores most activations in 4-bit format but keeps the outlier values in 8-bit format. It also designs a new GPU software routine (an optimized code path that runs on the GPU) that handles this mixed 4-bit/8-bit data efficiently by arranging the data in memory so the conversion from small integers back to usable numbers is fast, and by overlapping the data-loading and conversion steps with the actual math. The result is that a 70-billion-parameter model can run on a single 80 GB GPU with both reduced memory use and faster throughput.
